title: reviews group: per-session files, candidates jsonl, strict-vs-fail-open split, numeric locale sort, scoped git spawn
action: Port the reviews group: create, list, show, record, candidate.add, candidates, status (handlers packages/bee/bee.mjs:4300-4448; lib packages/bee/lib/reviews.mjs). Extend crates/bee-core/src/reviews.rs (976 LOC, today read-side). Preserve exactly: one JSON file per session at .bee/reviews/<id>.json written with writeJsonAtomic read-modify-write and NO cross-process lock; .bee/review-candidates.jsonl appended unlocked (reviews.mjs:357); the deliberate FAIL-LOUD vs FAIL-OPEN split (reviews.mjs:10-16) where mutation paths use readReviewStrict and throw on a corrupt session file while list/show skip-and-warn on the same file -- collapsing these to one policy is the exact regression this cell must not commit, so it needs its own scenario per side; the numeric locale sort at reviews.mjs:135, sessions.sort by String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id),'en',{numeric:true}), which orders review-2 before review-10 -- a plain byte sort is a red and needs a scenario whose ids separate the two orders; the scoped spawnSync git call at reviews.mjs:401 with cwd root and its test-seam indirection (:412) -- assert exact argv and cwd; the readCell dependency on lib/cells.mjs (reviews.mjs:23) for scope resolution, consumed from the already-ported crates/bee-core/src/cells.rs. Register --cmd-check scenarios: create/list/show/record round-trip; a corrupt session file fed to BOTH a mutation verb and list (opposite expected outcomes); ids review-1/review-2/review-10 present simultaneously; candidate.add and candidates on an empty and a corrupt-tail store; status derivation across unreviewed/in_review/reviewed/stale; the git argv assertion. ADVISOR-FOUND OBLIGATION: review-1/review-2/review-10 is too weak a scenario -- a hand-rolled natural sort passes it and still drifts from ICU numeric collation. localeCompare with numeric:true also decides LEADING-ZERO ties (review-01 versus review-1, numerically equal so the tiebreak itself is what is under test) and CASE (Review-2 versus review-2). Both must appear in the same scenario alongside the 1/2/10 ids, or the sort is not actually proven. REVIEW-FOUND GAP — the git-argv assertion had no stated mechanism, and the obvious one is a trap. defaultRunGit (packages/bee/lib/reviews.mjs:400) and its runGit seam (:412) are in-process node seams, unreachable from a cross-runtime argv diff. The only route is a PATH `git` shim both legs pick up that logs argv and cwd to a file, landing inside the diffed tree and OUTSIDE the exclusion prefixes at crates/bee-parity/src/differ.rs:28. State the chosen path in the worker block. SECOND REVIEW ITEM: crates/bee-core/src/cells.rs documents its own id sort as "a plain byte-order String compare, a deliberate narrowing of mjs localeCompare(id, en, {numeric:true})" — that is exactly the comparator class this cell exists to get right, so no cells.rs ordering helper may be reused for reviews id ordering. THIRD: the fixture generator zero-pads its ids so byte order equals numeric order (crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs), which means the sort scenario MUST seed its own non-padded ids via rpl-1 per-scenario seeding or it proves nothing. Also assert this group unknown-verb usage fallback line (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609). CARRIED FROM rpl-1: that cell was allowed to settle the numeric-string-key question either with a passing scenario or by recording that no ledger object can carry such keys. Its worker REFUTED the second option with evidence and settled it with a scenario, and the refutation lands here: `bee reviews record --kind manifest|preflight|decision|finding|uat` persists CALLER-SUPPLIED JSON into .bee/reviews/<id>.json UNSANITIZED (packages/bee/lib/reviews.mjs:283-327 via packages/bee/bee.mjs:4315-4322 and :4398-4404). Reviews is the ONLY one of the six groups where that is true -- every other counts/tally/group-by shape keys off a closed enum or renders to markdown. So this cell owes a scenario whose recorded payload carries integer-like object keys (e.g. "1", "2", "10") alongside non-numeric ones, proving the persisted file is byte-identical between runtimes: JS JSON.stringify hoists integer-like keys ascending while serde_json preserve_order keeps insertion order, and rpl-1 measured that exact divergence on a real store before fixing the emitter.

truths: cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group reviews reports every reviews scenario clean
the corrupt-session-file scenario proves BOTH sides: the mutation verb fails loudly and list skips-and-warns, identically in both runtimes
review-1/review-2/review-10 sort identically to mjs (numeric, not byte order)
the git argv and cwd match mjs exactly

the sort scenario contains review-01, review-1, Review-2, review-2 and review-10 simultaneously and the resulting order is byte-identical to mjs -- a hand-rolled natural sort that passes 1/2/10 alone is not acceptance
the git-argv log written by the shim lands inside the diffed tree and outside every exclusion prefix, proven by a negative control that alters the argv and IS caught
the sort scenario seeds its own non-zero-padded ids rather than relying on the generator padded ones
the reviews unknown-verb usage fallback line is byte-identical to mjs

a reviews record scenario persists a payload carrying integer-like object keys ("1","2","10") mixed with non-numeric ones, and the resulting .bee/reviews/<id>.json is byte-identical between runtimes — the numeric-string-key hazard rpl-1 refuted the escape hatch for

the workspace test run at the head of this cell verify is green with --no-fail-fast, so no cross-cutting pin has rotted outside every cell own gate (the rpl-3 goal-check found one that had been false for two cells because it sat outside every verify and was never executed)

prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No collapsing of the strict/fail-open split into one policy
No plain byte sort where mjs uses a numeric locale comparator
Tests never touch the live .bee/ store or run git in the repo root
No acceptance of the sort on the 1/2/10 case alone
No reuse of any crates/bee-core/src/cells.rs ordering helper for reviews id ordering — it is a documented byte-order narrowing
